newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk military demands prosecution of ex-minister.
newsitem.headline: Turk military demands prosecution of ex-minister.

text.p: Turkey's military leaders have demanded the prosecution of former interior minister Meral Aksener in an indictment sent to Ankara prosecutors on Tuesday, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

The agency said the chiefs of general staff had accused Aksener of "publicly insulting and mocking" the armed forces in a news conference she gave last week in which she admitted police had spied on the military.

Aksener said the police's surveillance operation against the secularist armed forces was carried out in order to pre-empt a possible coup against the Islamist-led government of which she was a member.
"(Police) intelligence service fulfilled a duty given by the laws...and democracy," she said at the news briefing.
A statement by the chiefs of staff at the time said Aksener's comments showed "a level of distrust between state organs never seen before in the history of the republic".

The charge, which carries a maximum sentence of six years imprisonment, must be approved by the justice ministry before it is passed on to parliament which would decide whether to lift the former minister's immunity from prosecution.
Turkey's first Islamist-led government collapsed three weeks ago after months of public wrangling with the powerful army over the administration's alleged backing of Islamic activism.
